# Results — Study 376 (MOC-Imbalance)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The folklore of the **closing
(market-on-close) auction**: large MOC **order imbalances** — biggest on index-rebalance
days, when passive funds must trade the official close — are said to **push the last print**
and then **reverse overnight**. No free auction-imbalance feed exists (the NYSE/Nasdaq MOC
imbalance message is a paid product), so we build a **transparent end-of-day-pressure
PROXY** from daily bars: each day's signed intraday **displacement** (where the close sits
in the day's range) stands in for "how hard price was pushed into the close." We then ask
the believers' question directly — does that push **reverse overnight** (close→open)?
Offline & deterministic; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily **raw** OHLC — SPY, QQQ, IWM (liquid, MOC-heavy index ETFs; public, no key) |
| Window | 2005-01-03 → 2026-06-17 (**16,194** ticker-days; **21.5** years; 5,398 sessions/ticker) |
| Pressure proxy | `disp = (close − open)/(high − low)`, clipped to [−1, 1]; **PROXY** for the closing-auction order imbalance |
| Overnight gap | `next_open / close − 1` (the close→open return the reversal is supposed to live in) |
| Rebalance subset | third Friday of quarter-end months (Mar/Jun/Sep/Dec) — **252** days, the largest real MOC imbalances |
| Entry / costs | 1-day execution lag is structural (enter today's close, gap realised at the **next** open); 2 bps one round-trip |

> **Proxy caveat (named on the Signal axis).** Intraday displacement is a *coarse, noisy*
> stand-in for a true closing-auction imbalance: it conflates the whole session's path with
> the final-print pressure the lore is about, and it carries the ETFs' own microstructure
> (bid-ask bounce at the open inflates apparent overnight reversal). The verdict does **not**
> hinge on the proxy's calibration — it hinges on the fact that even the *direction-correct*
> slope is statistically indistinguishable from noise, and **vanishes** on exactly the
> rebalance days where a real imbalance should bite hardest.

## The signal — does the close push reverse overnight?

Reversal regression `overnight ~ a + b·disp`. A robustly **negative** slope `b` is the
reversal the lore predicts (a big upward push into the close → a negative gap next morning).
HAC = Newey-West (5 lags); placebo p = share of 20,000 shuffled disp↔gap pairings whose
slope is **at least as negative** as observed.

| sample | n | slope `b` | HAC *t* | placebo *p* | corr(disp, gap) | fade win-rate |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **All days** | 16,194 | **−0.00017** | **−1.48** | 0.076 | −0.011 | 50.5% |
| **Rebalance days** (the strong case) | 252 | **−0.00044** | **−0.48** | 0.325 | −0.029 | 52.2% |
| SPY only | 5,398 | −0.00027 | −1.54 | 0.072 | −0.020 | 50.9% |
| QQQ only | 5,398 | −0.00010 | −0.64 | 0.266 | −0.009 | 49.3% |
| IWM only | 5,398 | −0.00009 | −0.49 | 0.316 | −0.007 | 51.3% |

Read it carefully. The slope **has the lore's sign** — it is *negative*, i.e. a push into
the close does lean back overnight on average. But on the full tape the HAC **t = −1.48**
(placebo p = 0.076) **fails the t ≥ 2 bar**, the correlation is **−0.011** (the push explains
~0.01% of the overnight gap's variance), and the fade win-rate is **50.5%** — a coin flip.
Crucially, on the **index-rebalance subset** — where the believers say the imbalance is
*largest* — the effect **gets weaker, not stronger**: **t = −0.48, p = 0.33**. A real
imbalance edge should concentrate exactly there; instead it disappears.

## Tradability — the fade is a rounding error that costs flip negative

Fade strategy: take position −sign(disp) into the close (fade the push), earn the next
overnight gap. The 1-day lag is structural (entry = today's close, exit = next open).

| cost (round-trip) | mean / trade | annualised (if run daily) |
|---|--:|--:|
| **0 bps (gross)** | **+0.18 bps** | +0.46% |
| 1 bp | −0.82 bps | −2.04% |
| **2 bps** | **−1.82 bps** | **−4.48%** |

Even **gross**, the fade earns **+0.18 bps per trade** (daily Sharpe ≈ **0.04**) — a rounding
error, not an edge. A 1-bp round-trip already pushes it **negative**; at a realistic 2 bps it
loses **−4.5%/yr**. The "free overnight snap-back" is **inside the spread**: the apparent
reversal is the kind of microstructure noise that a market-maker captures and a taker pays
for. On rebalance days the gross is larger (+2.4 bps) but on **252 days in 21 years** — once a
quarter — it is not a NAV-scale strategy, and net of cost it is +0.4 bps on a coin flip.

## Synthetic positive control — the engine is faithful, and zero edge stays zero

A deterministic OHLC panel with a **planted overnight-reversal knob**: a fraction `reversal`
of each day's into-the-close push is mechanically faded next overnight. The detector +
inference must recover it and must **not** invent significance when the knob is off.

| planted reversal | n | slope `b` | corr | HAC *t* | placebo *p* | fade win-rate |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **0.00** (no edge) | 4,000 | −0.00003 | −0.003 | **−0.20** | 0.416 | 51.1% |
| **0.10** (large edge) | 4,000 | −0.00111 | −0.130 | **−8.10** | 0.000 | 55.6% |

With **no** planted reversal the test sits at **t = −0.20** — it does not manufacture
significance from noise. A planted reversal lights up monotonically (a mere 5% fade already
gives t = −4.2; 10% gives **t = −8.1**, p < 0.001). The control proves the engine is unbiased
and *powerful* — so the real-tape **t = −1.48** is not a power failure: it is what a
**near-zero** true reversal looks like through a faithful, well-powered lens.

## Verdict

- **Signal — WEAK.** The slope is *direction-correct* (negative: pushes do lean back
  overnight) but **fails the t ≥ 2 bar** on the real tape (HAC **t = −1.48**, placebo
  p = 0.076), explains ~0.01% of variance, and — decisively — **weakens on the
  index-rebalance days where the lore says it should be strongest** (t = −0.48). A
  faint-but-insignificant, proxy-based, non-robust whisper ⇒ **WEAK**, not REAL. (Proxy +
  survivorship-free ETFs named on the axis; the proxy can only *over*-state reversal via the
  open's bid-ask bounce, so the true effect is weaker still.)
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Gross fade is **+0.18 bps/trade** (Sharpe ≈ 0.04); a 1-bp
  round-trip turns it **negative**, 2 bps loses **−4.5%/yr**. The "overnight snap-back" lives
  **inside the spread** — captured by the auction's liquidity providers, paid by anyone who
  crosses it. Not deployable.
- **Free lunch? — BUSTED.** The closing-auction-imbalance reversal is *real-as-microstructure*
  and *empty-as-alpha*: a tiny, correct-sign effect that the bid-ask spread eats whole, and
  that evaporates precisely on the rebalance days believers point to.
